newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures sell off late, end down.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures sell off late, end down.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures sold off late in the day, jerked awake by profit-taking after a session of consolidation in most indices.
Traders said the technology sector led losses as investors rushed to liquidate long positions after several sessions of strong gains.
Nervousness tied to upcoming corporate earnings releases and sluggish Treasury bond futures exacerbated declines.
U.S. December Standard and Poor 500s hit a contract and all-time high early at 710.60, hovered near unchanged midday and sold off late to key support at 704.40 late.

Early in the session, December Nasdaq 100 futures soared to a third consecutive contract and record high on bullishness in the semiconductor sector after optimistic comments from a Merrill Lynch analyst. But later, Salomon Brothers downgraded Intel Corp. to hold from a strong buy, stoking profit-taking.
"The Nasdaq dragged us down late," an S&P 500 futures trader said. "They turned around about midday and that's what led us lower," he added.
In December S&Ps sellstops were triggered below 706.00, he said.
